title: Low-noise launch microprotocol — evening stability lane (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, low-noise release microprotocol intended for evening/after-hours launches where minimizing user-visible impact and operator churn is the priority. It combines a narrow traffic ramp, tight observability gates, and a 4-hour steward window followed by an automated quiet-handoff. Use this when feature surface is scoped (small config/flag, model pin, routing tweak) and there are no major infra migrations.

Scope and assumptions:
- Small surface change: config flag, routing policy tweak, model variant swap (quantized variant), or small routing rule.
- Expected customer impact: negligible to low; still treat as potentially customer-facing.
- Canary traffic: 0.5% initial, linear ramp to 5% over 30 minutes if all gates green.
- Required on-call coverage: 1 steward (release engineer) + 1 SRE watcher for first 2 hours, then steward only.

Key objectives:
- Zero/near-zero user errors during rollout.
- Keep latency 99th within +15% of baseline.
- Detect regressions within 5 minutes of occurrence.

Before the evening window (T-72h to T-1h checklist):
- T-72h: Finalize PR and release-note snippet (owner: Maya). Link: PR#3124.
- T-48h: Smoke tests: nightly gating must pass on staging (build id + tag).
- T-24h: Confirm rollback plan documented (RELEASE-1243).
- T-6h: Confirm on-call rotations and pager tags. Slack channel: #release-evening.
- T-2h: Generate a small synthetic load test for the exact traffic shape. Note: use -stability/loadgen/sample-quiet.yaml.
- T-30m: Snapshot telemetry baseline for last 24h (latency percentiles, error rate, token throughput). Save snapshot in artifacts.
- T-15m: Notify support and product (template below).

Evening microprotocol timeline (minute-by-minute, local times relative to start):
- T-00: Start window. Declare watch in Slack: @here "Starting low-noise launch window. Steward: Maya. SRE: Ethan (first 2h)."
- T+02:00m: Deploy config/flag/model variant to canary pool (0.5% traffic). Wait 5m for stable KV caches and warmup.
- T+07m: First observability check (automated): error rate, 95/99/999 latency, token p50/p95/p99, request CPU/GPU queue metrics.
- T+10m: Manual quick-check: run 20 `smoke-request` calls against canary endpoint, sample outputs for hallucination/noise.
- T+15m: If all checks green, ramp to 1.5% over 5 minutes. If any gate fails, roll back to previous config immediately and notify.
- T+25m: Checkpoint: hold for 10 minutes. Run traffic-slice tests for common customer flows (embedding, chat, function-call) — owner: Liam.
- T+35m: If green, ramp to 3.0% over 10 minutes.
- T+50m: Hold for 10 min, run automated regression evals on pre-curated prompt set (eval job ID: eval-evening-0626).
- T+70m: Ramp to 5% over 15 minutes if all gates green.
- T+95m: Start slow regional scale validation: simulate regional imbalance (10% more traffic in EU) for 5 minutes and validate routing fallback.
- T+110m: Steward decision point: promote to global gradual rollout or revert. If promote, schedule automated 1hr incremental ramp policy.
- T+180m: If stable, trigger quiet-handoff: notify product/support and place change into monitoring-only mode for 24h.

Fast rollback triggers (immediate rollback):
- Sustained error spike > 0.5% absolute over baseline for 3 consecutive 1-min buckets.
- Latency p99 > baseline + 25% for > 5 minutes.
- Utility regressions on eval set (f1/drop > threshold) or obvious semantic failure (top-3 hallucinations on smoke requests).
- Sustained resource saturation (GPU queue depth > 80% for 5m).

Quick actions on rollback:
- Revert config flag or model variant in canary group immediately (automated revert script: release-revert.sh).
- Post rollback: collect 30m of telemetry, tag snapshot, open incident stub in RELEASE-1243-RB with initial logs & stack dumps.
- Notify stakeholders in Slack + email template.

Observability gates (automated monitors):
- metric: endpoint.errors.total (alert if rate > baseline + 0.5% absolute)
- metric: endpoint.latency.p99 (alert if > baseline * 1.25)
- metric: gpu.queue_depth (alert if > 80%)
- log-based: downstream-timeout errors (count > 5 in 10m window)
- eval-based: nightly-eval.regression-score (alert if drop > 3 points)

Post-release quick notes (to fill in within 2h of quiet-handoff):
- Performance summary: baseline vs observed (p50/p95/p99, tokens/s).
- Errors: count and user-facing incidents.
- Model quality: short summary from regression evals + examples.
- Operator actions: any manual fixes, warm-cache nudges.
- Learning / TODOs for next night: prune long-running checks, add a synthetic scenario for regional burst.

Draft release-note blurb (customer-facing, short):
- "Deploying a small performance and routing tweak to improve inference stability for low-latency customers. No action required. If you notice errors or latency regressions, contact support@redwood.ai or open a ticket with ID RELEASE-1243."

Short support message (internal to product/support):
- Subject: Evening low-noise launch (RELEASE-1243) — expected low impact
- Body: Short description of change, stewardship names, rollback criteria, support playbook snippet. Attach the short smoke script for reproducing errors.

Operator cheat-sheet (commands):
- Promote canary: ./ci/deploy_canary.sh --tag canary-3124 --pct 0.5
- Ramp: ./ci/ramp_pct.sh --target 5 --duration 30m
- Revert: ./ops/release-revert.sh --release RELEASE-1243 --reason "auto-gate-failure"
- Snapshot telemetry: ./tools/snap_baseline.sh --name evening-0626

Unresolved questions / open items (notes-to-self):
- Do we want to auto-inflate request timeouts by 10% during first 20m of canary to avoid false positives? (ask SRE)
- Are there any downstream partners with strict rate limits that need a pre-notify? (email: partners@redwood.ai)
- Add an integration test for the regional imbalance scenario — assigned to Priya.

Postmortem template (if rollback occurs):
- Timeline (minute-level)
- Root cause hypothesis + evidence from logs and evals
- Why the canary gates missed detection (if applicable)
- Corrective actions & owners (3-point plan)
- Customer communications timeline and follow-ups

Quick references and links:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3124
- Issue: RELEASE-1243
- Eval job: eval-evening-0626

Raw notes / scratchpad (freeform):
- 2026-06-10 18:12 Maya: quick thought — warm cache by pinging stale endpoints with small prompt set (30 reqs) at T+03m to reduce cold-kv noise.
- 2026-06-11 09:03 Ethan: added a watch rule for downstream timeout logs -> see rule id watch-rt-42.
- 2026-06-12 14:50 Priya: will add regional imbalance simulation to nightly harness; ETA 2026-06-18.

USE CASE NOTES: This microprotocol is intentionally lightweight. If the change touches schema migrations, storage, or broad model architecture swaps, revert to the full release runbook and extended rollback matrix.

End of draft. Fill in the post-release summary section within 2 hours of quiet-handoff and tag RELEASE-1243 for follow-up retrospective.
